what_it_is: Airbus Defence and Space is the military-aircraft and space division of Airbus SE, producing the C295 transport, A400M airlifter, Eurofighter (via the consortium) and military satellites and communications. In India its flagship programme is the C295: 56 aircraft contracted in 2021, with Tata Advanced Systems building a final assembly line in Vadodara - the first military aircraft assembly line of its kind in India.
india_angle: India formally acquired 56 C295s in September 2021 under a government-to-government framework; 16 fly-away aircraft arrive from Spain and 40 are assembled by Tata Advanced Systems in Vadodara with more than 85% structural work targeted in India. The first Indian-built C295 was inducted in 2025 with the line inaugurated by the prime ministers of India and Spain.
intelligence_assessment: The C295 programme is among the most verifiable Make-in-India military-aerospace programmes, anchored by Airbus and Government of India releases. Watch the Baroda line's delivery cadence, the promised 40-aircraft indigenisation ramp and follow-on C295 maritime-derivative discussion as the key evidence stream.

faq.q: How many C295 aircraft is India buying?
faq.a: 56 - sixteen delivered fly-away from Spain and forty assembled at Tata Advanced Systems' Vadodara line.

faq.q: Where is the Indian C295 assembly line?
faq.a: Vadodara, Gujarat - operated by Tata Advanced Systems with Airbus; inaugurated in October 2024.
